slides.title: Research Proposal
slides.text:
Research Proposal

Context: Substantial research have been made into the development of autoregressive 3D generative models, i.e. MeshGPT and followed by a series of variant and improved models.

What’s inside the black box?

GIF: Demonstration of autoregressively generating triangular meshes

slides.title: Research Proposal
slides.text:
Research Proposal

The Gap: 
There is no published study of what individual attention head do in mesh generation transformers. Recent models are developed with assumptions of attention mechanisms rather than systematically and quantitatively measuring it. 
Opportunity: 
In language models, measuring attention head behavior led directly to a design of faster decoding and memory caching features. DuoAttention (ICLR 2025). 
The same approach and inspiration can be applied to enhance autoregressive mesh transformers. 

How to interpret 3D Autoregressive Mesh Transformers?

We examine the question of what query triangles attend to in the early token sequence, and why?

slides.title: Experimental Method
slides.text:
Experimental Method


Choose 500 ShapeNet shapes from 5 shape categories: chair, table, airplane, bottle, lamp
Choose 4 model families to experiment with: 
MeshGPT: learned-codebook decoder only transformer 
MeshXL: raw coordinate prediction decoder only transformer
DeepMesh: “Point-cloud to mesh” generators with hourglass transformer structure
MeshMosaic: “Part by part” mesh generators, generates in small patches and fuses together into one mesh object

Data Set & Model of Choice

5 categories of shape examined

slides.title: Experimental Method
slides.text:
Experimental Method 

Compare: for each head, compare what category (cluster) of triangles do the attended triangles fall into.
Potentially find generalizable patterns across the 4 models 

Feed: run inference by passing 500 ShapeNet meshes into each model in one forward pass

Record: at one query triangle, save the attention weight each head gives to every earlier triangle

Select:  select attended triangles that holds significant attention weight assigned by a head.

Group: group ShapeNet triangles into clusters by different their triangle properties

Model Enhancements：
Hard code attention head with rules/policies
 Etc…

slides.title: Experimental Method
slides.text:
Experimental Method

Active-Dormant head classification: 
Dormant heads attend largely to the “beginning of sequence” token or to the very first few tokens of the token sequence. 
Active heads pay attention to nearby tokens, or any tokens that are not the BOS or initial tokens. 

Examining “active” attention heads

MeshGPT: most attention heads become ‘active’ at earlier layers and become ‘dormant’ at later layers.

We examine ‘active’ heads as they present more informative insights by attending to a variety of tokens / triangles

slides.title: Experimental Method
slides.text:
Experimental Method

Selection of triangles for examination:
Cluster the 500 chosen shapes by their triangular mesh features: Aspect Ratio, Area, X-axis, Y-axis, and Z-axis normal vector orientation into 5 clusters for each property.
Compare which of clusters do the attended triangles fall into.

slides.title: Current Findings (WIP)
slides.text:
Current Findings (WIP)

TLDR

Across the four models, individual attention heads show tendencies to prefer specific shapes of triangles. (differing by the model, head, and transformer layer)
I.e. certain heads strongly favor large area triangles and some other favor thin and elongated shaped triangles.
These shape preferences have been shown to be consistent at different query positions across the entire generated mesh token sequence. 
These behaviors are inconsistent across different transformer layers (we classify into early, middle, and late layers)

slides.title: Extending the work
slides.text:
Extending the work

Fine-tune 3D generators to generate artist quality mesh 
Amplify certain head behavior, injecting a prior/bias to certain heads to force them to produce consistent attention preference.
Hard-coding programmable rules on attention heads
For heads that demonstrate consistent preference, hard-code their behavior into rules/policies to reduce computational expensiveness or potentially leading to better generation quality.
The why question
Why does the model choose to attend to such features? 
Challenges
Retraining/fine-tuning can be computationally expensive
Uncertainty about which methods would be beneficial
